hints: Remember that any ester is made from a carboxylic acid plus an alcohol, so look for both of those functional groups in one molecule.
Count the atoms in the delta lactone ring, it has five carbons and one oxygen, so the open chain must have the same carbon skeleton.
Join the $\text{-OH}$ end to the $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ end with loss of water, and check which chain length closes neatly to give that six-membered ring.
walkthrough:
**Recognise what a lactone is**

Think of delta lactone as an internal ester. Normally an ester forms like this:

$$\text{RCO}_2\text{H} + \text{R'OH} \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2\text{R'} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Here both groups are in the same molecule, so a hydroxy-acid can cyclise in one step.

**Count the ring size needed**

Look at the diagram. The ring contains one $\text{C=O}$ carbon, three $\text{CH}_2$ groups plus one more $\text{CH}_2$ next to O, and one O. That is 5 carbons + 1 oxygen = a 6-membered ring.

So the open-chain precursor must contain 5 carbons in a row, with $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ at one end and $\text{-OH}$ at the other.

**Match to the options**

$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is 5-hydroxypentanoic acid. Its $\text{-OH}$ can attack its own $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ to lose $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and close the exact 6-membered lactone:

$$\text{HO(CH}_2\text{)}_4\text{CO}_2\text{H} \rightarrow \text{delta lactone} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

options.A: Contains $\text{-OH}$ and $\text{-CHO}$ (aldehyde), not $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$. An aldehyde plus alcohol would give a cyclic hemiacetal, not a cyclic ester. You need a carboxylic acid to make an ester linkage.
options.B: $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ has both an alcohol and a carboxylic acid on a 5-carbon chain. Intramolecular esterification loses water and forms the 6-membered cyclic ester shown, exactly delta lactone.
options.C: Contains two $\text{-OH}$ groups ($\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) but no carboxylic acid. A diol cannot form an ester on its own, it would need a dicarboxylic acid to make polyester.
options.D: $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is a 6-hydroxy acid with one extra $\text{CH}_2$. Cyclisation would give a 7-membered ring, not the 6-membered delta lactone. This is the classic chain-length trap.
